title: Don Dunbar's modern band
summary: He joins Don Dunbar's more modern band with written arrangements, and lists its sidemen and sharp uniforms.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I had another opportunity to play with a very fine band around home. The other band was just more modern than Doc's band. It had more special arrangements, we called it in those days. They had several good writers in there. Don Dunbar, whose real name was Lawrence Jefferson, he taught music at Howard University and he was a very fine writer, but he'd come back home and put a band together. He had very good arrangements. He had a fine guitar player that
was writing at the time, and maybe his name will come to me... Robert E. Lee, that's his name. Robert E. Lee, a fine, fine guitar player and writer. So they had a lot of arrangements, you know...
Oh, during those days guys would change them for stage reasons. You know, they'd change their names around. But that was a very good.
Doc Palmer's band played all stocks?

No, they had some special arrangements. But this band had more writers. They had a lot of writers in it. And it was a little more modern band than Doc's band. So they asked me if I would like to play in the band, and so that was a lovely experience to be able to play that music. And they had a very, very good band. I remember some of the guys... Zeke Bradley, a good trumpet player, played with that band. Another fine trumpet player, J.W. Barnes. A good trombone player, Lawrence Johnson. They had a girl piano player, Micki Gwynn ...(?). And there was a saxophone player, an alto player named Bolden(?) Townsend. And Simon(?) Jefferson, a guy with a great big tone on the tenor saxophone; he had a great big tone on the tenor saxophone, a la Chu Berry. And we had...Billy Jones played the drums, and Doug(?)/Dump(?)/Doc(?) Harvey played the

bass.
That was a very good band, the first band where we really had real sharp uniforms and everything that I played with. You know, that was a (?)really big deal(?).
You were how old when you played with them?
